summary.headline: City Union Bank Q2 FY27 PAT rose 27% YoY to INR 416 crores, with advances up 26% to INR 72,442 crores and Gross NPA down to 1.44%.
summary.overview: Management reported a strong Q2 FY27: advances grew over INR 4,800 crores QoQ (over 7%) to INR 72,442 crores, deposits rose 21% YoY to INR 83,893 crores, and NIM expanded 9 bps QoQ to 3.87%. Asset quality improved sharply, helped by sale of INR 803 crores of technically written-off and live accounts to an ARC, with Gross NPA falling to 1.44% from 1.73%. Management guided NIM to 3.85-3.95% for Q3 and Q4, and addressed scrutiny on gold loan practices, LTV norms and ECL transition impact (about INR 300 crores, of which about INR 30 crores already provided).

financial_highlights.change: Up from 3.78% in Q1 FY27; H1 FY26 was 3.59%
Down from 1.73% in Q1 FY27 (29 bps); Net NPA 0.48% vs 0.9% a year ago
+35% YoY from INR 259 crores; includes ARC-related income
Created as buffer for economic uncertainty

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances rose INR 2,600 crores QoQ to INR 42,862 crores from INR 40,262 crores; management calls it the core strength. Utilisation of SME lines is about 71-72%, up from 69% last quarter.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book rose INR 1,062 crores QoQ to INR 21,777 crores from INR 20,715 crores; about 30% of advances. Agri is about 50% of customers; 96% of the book is in South India; blended yield about 10.8%. Gold SMA-2 at about INR 173 crores (0.24% of gold advances).

segments.name: Secured retail loans
segments.commentary: Secured retail advances rose INR 1,134 crores QoQ to INR 7,802 crores from INR 6,668 crores.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: Treasury income was INR 36 crores in Q2 vs INR 52 crores in Q1; about INR 12 crores of mutual fund income was reclassified to interest income after the bank exited its MF holdings.

guidance_outlook: NIM guided to 3.85% to 3.95% for Q3 and Q4 FY27, supported by repricing of about 55% EBLR-linked loans after recent policy rate changes.
Deposit cost expected to rise about 10 bps in the next quarter; deposit rates had not yet moved as liquidity remained ample.
ROA expected to move above 1.6% (management also cited a 1.6-1.65% range on closing).
Cost-to-income expected at 45-47% for FY27; quarterly staff cost run rate of about INR 275-280 crores going forward.
Credit growth targeted at 2-3 percentage points above industry; deposit growth to stay aligned with credit growth.
Tax rate expected at 21-23% going forward, a blended 22-23% for the year; ECL transition impact about INR 300 crores, with management saying no P&L impact as it is adjusted against capital.
capex_capacity: Branch network grew from about 800 to over 1,000 branches; newly opened branches are reported to be contributing consistently.
Gold loans are offered from 250-260 branches, mainly rural and semi-urban; a typical branch book is INR 40-50 crores.
Deposit verticalisation launched across salary, TASC, government, CASA and NRI segments.
demand_pricing: Deposits grew 21% YoY; CASA ratio stable at 27%; average CD ratio 86%. Term deposits below INR 3 crores are 48% of the book, INR 3-50 crores 17%, and above INR 50 crores 8%.
Bank took FCNR deposits of USD 69 million under the RBI swap window (USD 15 million from new-to-bank customers), swapped into rupees and deployed domestically.
Gold loan yields are rising on fixed-rate book repricing; management sees 5-10 bps more headroom from loan renewals. Agri vs non-agri yield differential about 100 bps.
Average ticket size per account: gold agri INR 1.90 lakhs, gold non-agri INR 3 lakhs; retail INR 70-80 lakhs excluding Mumbai and Delhi.
Management said 20% deposit growth would be hard to sustain over the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan scrutiny: how was INR 9.5 crores of gold NPA resolved, and what is the loan structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Only INR 20 lakhs of the INR 9.5 crores NPA went to auction; the rest was repaid by borrowers. 99% of consumption loans are bullet, with no change in behaviour seen. The bank does not do top-ups, and says it does not finance NPAs.

qa_highlights.question: Why were the technically written-off accounts sold to the ARC at 16% cash recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 803 crores sold (INR 131 crores consideration; INR 792 crores provided). About INR 740 crores were over three years old, including 757 loans of INR 645 crores over five years. INR 303 crores was secured and INR 500 crores unsecured. TW pool outstanding is INR 900 crores, fully provided; no reversal taken.

qa_highlights.question: Is the staff cost increase one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly the July wage revision, plus INR 32 crores of leave encashment provision in Q2 against a normal INR 3-5 crores. Run rate is INR 275-280 crores per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 and Q2 were 23-24% because of write-offs; the going-forward range is 21-23%, around 22-23% blended.

qa_highlights.question: Quantum of ECL transition impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental ECL requirement at 30 Sep 2026 is INR 299.42 crores, down from INR 445 crores at 31 Mar 2025. About INR 30 crores already provided and INR 20 crores adjusted against capital; the remaining is to be absorbed in capital.

qa_highlights.question: Will deposit growth of 20% be sustainable in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management was doubtful about 20% growth over the next two years. Granularity is improving and new branches are contributing, but it said it needs more time to confirm.

risks_watch: Gold loan quality: sharp gold price correction could strain LTV cushions; SMA-0/1/2 totalled 2.53% of gross advances.
Asset quality reliance on recoveries and ARC sales; the TW pool and recoveries will need watching.
Deposit cost rise of about 10 bps next quarter could compress the NIM guidance if lending repricing lags.
Deposit growth sustainability against competition, with management doubtful about 20% growth.
Treasury/AFS mark-to-market: bond MTM loss sits in AFS reserve; CFO to share figures later.
Contingent provisioning and ECL transition impact (about INR 270 crores net unprovided) to be absorbed through capital.
summary.management_tone: Confident and detailed on growth, NIM and asset quality, with management saying the quarter was in line with or above expectations. It was defensive on gold loan practices, giving detailed LTV and end-use explanations. It was openly cautious on FY28 deposit growth of 20%.
key_quotes: We have achieved 25% credit growth for the last three quarters consecutively.
Our Gross NPA percentage has reduced to 1.44% in 2QFY27 from 1.73% in 1QFY27 which is 29 bps reduction.
So 20% in the next two years, I think I would be doubtful, sir.
Our cost-to-income will largely be in the range of 45% to 47% for FY27.

adds.what: Branch network expanded from about 800 to over 1,000 branches (already opened, contributing)

growth.why: Management guides NIM of 3.85-3.95% for Q3-Q4 FY27 on repricing of about 55% EBLR-linked loans, and credit growth 2-3 pp above industry, backed by advances up 26% YoY to INR 72,442 crores and a branch network grown from about 800 to over 1,000; no explicit revenue growth number was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM guided to 3.85-3.95% for Q3-Q4 vs 3.87% in Q2 and 3.78% in Q1, supported by repricing of about 55% EBLR-linked loans, but a 10 bps deposit cost rise next quarter could offset it.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branches grew from about 800 to over 1,000 and gold loans are offered from 250-260 branches; no new branch target was quantified, so further expansion is probable but not guided with numbers.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Advances up 26% YoY to INR 72,442 crores and targeted to grow 2-3 pp above industry, though management doubts 20% deposit growth can be sustained for two years.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: NIM guidance of 3.85-3.95% and cost-to-income of 45-47% for FY27 are framed as the base case, with Q2 NIM at 3.87% and Q2 cost-to-income at 45.96%; no explicit revenue upgrade was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Deposit cost up about 10 bps next quarter, gold price correction risk to LTVs, and SMA-0/1/2 at 2.53% of gross advances could compress NIM or raise provisions.

rows.label: ECL transition absorbed through capital
rows.why: Incremental ECL requirement of INR 299.42 crores at 30 Sep 2026, with about INR 30 crores provided and INR 20 crores adjusted against capital, so about INR 270 crores remains to be absorbed in capital with no P&L impact per management.

rows.label: Deposit verticalisation and CASA push
rows.why: Deposits up 21% YoY to INR 83,893 crores with CASA stable at 27% and verticalisation launched across salary, TASC, government, CASA and NRI segments; management cautious on sustaining 20% growth.

rows.label: Gold loan book growth in South India
rows.why: Gold book rose INR 1,062 crores QoQ to INR 21,777 crores (about 30% of advances), with 96% in South India and blended yield about 10.8%, with 5-10 bps further yield headroom from renewals.

tone.note: Management was confident on NIM, growth and asset quality, and cautious on FY28 deposit growth of 20% and defensive on gold loan LTV and end-use practices; analysts pushed on gold loan scrutiny, the ARC sale economics and the ECL transition impact.
